prize_parts.citation: for the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that enable the delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are rational molecular design with a measurable consequence for what clinicians can do. Cullis, Hope and Madden showed that a lipid whose charge is tuned by pKa (neutral in blood, protonated in the endosome) together with PEG-lipid control of particle size and controlled mixing can encapsulate and deliver nucleic acids. Without this chemistry neither patisiran nor the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines would exist in usable form. It rests on lipid phase behaviour and self-assembly, so it is chemistry in substance and not only an application. It also covers delivery, which the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification did not, and several independent groups and years of approved products have confirmed it. Sparr, whose field is lipid self-assembly, reached the same view independently and ranked it second, which I take as a check on my own bias toward translational work.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Delivery chemistry was built by academic and company groups together (MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and later industrial optimizers of ionizable lipids), and a Vancouver trio may read as a judgment about patents and priority more than a clean scientific boundary. A second concern is that the committee may see a delivery vehicle so soon after the 2023 Medicine prize as a decoration of a prize already given. A third is that I rank this first partly because it fits my own translational outlook, and I may be overweighting clinical impact relative to the discovery of a new chemical principle.

responses.point: Sparr ranks B064 second as lipid self-assembly applied to a transformative problem, with pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, and stresses strong independent validation but notes that credit is split between academic and company work and that the 2023 Medicine prize creates an overlap question.
responses.response: I agree on the physical chemistry and on the overlap question, and I think the overlap is smaller than it looks. The 2023 prize rewarded what the RNA is made of (nucleoside modification to avoid innate sensing), while this work rewards how it reaches the cytosol, which is a lipid phase, pKa and endosomal-escape problem. I would still welcome your view on whether Vancouver's early formulation work or later lipid-library screening is the more fundamental step, because that decides whether the trio holds.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B008 first because induced degradation turns ubiquitin-proteasome biology into a designable chemical reaction, and ranks B064 seventh with Cullis, Hope and Anderson, mainly because credit is spread across academic and company groups.
responses.response: I take the attribution objection seriously, and I keep Anderson out only because the lipidoid and screening work came after the ionizable-lipid concept and formulation methods. On B008 I accept the mechanism is elegant, but I put degraders below LNPs because no PROTAC is yet approved, while LNP-based medicines are used on billions of people. If the committee prefers more evidence in hand, maturity favours B064 over B008.

responses.point: Åqvist ranks B058 first, framing base editing as chemistry on a nucleobase through evolved deaminases, with Liu alone as the cleanest configuration given the 2020 CRISPR prize, and does not rank B064 at all.
responses.response: I agree that base editing is a real chemical design and I keep it as my first alternative. My disagreement is about timing and breadth. Its clinical record is short and the 2020 prize makes it a follow-on to genome editing, while LNPs enabled a whole class of medicines. I would not object to a Liu-led B058 if the committee wants a single clean laureate, but I do not think that attribution advantage outweighs the evidence of impact from B064.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B030 first as Buchwald and Hartwig's ligand-controlled Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling, with very broad use in synthesis and a clean two-person prize that extends the 2010 cross-coupling recognition.
responses.response: I accept this is the cleanest attribution and the most mature case on the list, and as a non-synthetic chemist I defer to you and Zou on the ligand design details. My reservation is that it extends a theme already honoured in 2010, so I read it as an incremental extension of recognized chemistry, whereas B064 opens a new area. That is a judgment about novelty of principle, not a claim that B030 is less rigorous.

uncertainties: Whether the founding ionizable-lipid and formulation work is separable from later lipidoid and screening contributions (Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan) so that a Cullis, Hope and Madden trio is defensible.
How much weight the committee should give to the 2023 Medicine prize when judging whether delivery chemistry is distinct enough.
My knowledge of the early Vancouver priority record comes from memory and has not been checked against primary sources.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. I have no known ties to Vancouver, to the LNP groups or companies, or to the other shortlisted candidates, but my biosensor spin-out and clinical collaborations make me favour translational impact, which I flag as a bias and not a recusal issue.
